pack.name: Fworld Original: The Sograt Letter
pack.description: Short original places, people, history, and activities for the sample story.

entries.name: The Sograt Road
entries.summary: A dry route links the capital gate, Morroc, and several landmarks.
entries.body: In this original setting, travelers leave short route notes at staffed gates and shaded stops. The road's useful knowledge is practical: water, turns, and who last carried a parcel.

entries.name: Prontera
entries.summary: A walled city gate where outbound parcels and traveler questions are entered in a small ledger.
entries.body: In this original version of the story, the quiet gate is a place to check the day's deliveries, ask about road conditions, and compare written route notes.

entries.name: Morroc
entries.summary: A compact town where the main road meets market errands and local travel notes.
entries.body: Travelers pause here to refill water and compare directions. Local advice tends to name a landmark rather than promise a precise distance.

entries.name: Morroc Market
entries.summary: A close-packed market where sellers and runners exchange practical travel goods and small messages.
entries.body: Stallholders keep their own short notes for unclaimed parcels and receipts. A blank line on a slip is often an invitation to ask, not proof that a delivery was lost.

entries.name: The Pyramid
entries.summary: A stone landmark beyond a marked trail from Morroc, with a scout watching the approach.
entries.body: Visitors check the trail marker before moving farther from town. In this original account, the structure is simply a landmark on the route; its details come from what travelers observe here.

entries.name: Sograt
entries.summary: An open stretch of hot road where travelers plan shaded rests.
entries.body: People cross in short stages, using a few familiar patches of shade. A cup of water and an honest estimate of the next stop matter more than a hurried pace.

entries.name: Morroc's Shared Road Ledger
entries.summary: Morroc's route notes grew from practical records of water stops and parcel handoffs.
entries.body: Local tellers say the first shared ledger began after two couriers arrived with matching notes but different last-mile directions. Its keeper began recording landmarks and handoffs, not names, so travelers could correct a route without claiming another person's story.

entries.name: Check the Gate Ledger
entries.summary: Compare the day's outbound entries with a courier's route note.
entries.body: Ask the gate keeper to read the relevant entries aloud, then compare their times and parcel marks with a route strip. The ledger records what was written, not what a traveler meant.

entries.name: Compare Morroc Route Notes
entries.summary: Compare familiar landmarks and water stops with a local travel note.
entries.body: A traveler can ask which landmark a note refers to and whether the water stop is still usable. Different accounts can be checked side by side without assuming either person is mistaken.

entries.name: Ask About an Unclaimed Receipt
entries.summary: Ask a stallholder whether a blank receipt line matches an ordinary market handoff.
entries.body: A visitor can ask which stall issued a receipt and whether its blank note line was meant for a later name. The answer comes from the seller's record and the details of that handoff.

entries.name: Read the Pyramid Trail Marker
entries.summary: Read the trail marker and note which turn leads back toward Morroc.
entries.body: The scout can point out the return marker and explain how its lettering distinguishes the townward path from the farther trail. Visitors are free to pause and ask before continuing.

entries.name: Plan a Shaded Rest
entries.summary: Compare the next stretch with the shaded places used by local travelers.
entries.body: A guide can describe the shade along the route and help estimate a comfortable pause. Travelers decide for themselves when to stop and how much water to carry.

entries.name: Edrin
entries.summary: A patient ledger keeper at the Prontera gate who prefers dates and parcel marks to guesses.
entries.body: Edrin handles questions about the day's outbound entries in a formal, patient manner. He asks travelers to distinguish what they saw from what they were told.

entries.name: Sava
entries.summary: A practical gate keeper who checks travelers arriving by the Morroc road.
entries.body: Sava keeps the arrival line moving and answers direct questions about local routes. A clear landmark is more useful to Sava than a confident but vague direction.

entries.name: Nima
entries.summary: A cheerful market seller who keeps an eye on useful travel goods and unclaimed slips.
entries.body: Nima knows which stalls handle ordinary supplies and is quick to notice when a receipt has been left without a name. She prefers a specific question to a broad guess about the market.

entries.name: Piri
entries.summary: A quick market runner who carries short errands between stalls.
entries.body: Piri is curious about small details and moves easily through the busy aisles. Give Piri a stall, a color, or a time to narrow down an errand.

entries.name: Teren
entries.summary: A steady scout near the Pyramid trail who points out the return marker.
entries.body: Teren keeps visitors oriented near the approach and would rather guide someone back before dusk than hurry them farther along the trail.

entries.name: Ami
entries.summary: A kind route guide who remembers shaded rest points across Sograt.
entries.body: Ami gives careful advice about where travelers can pause and listens for the conditions of the road that day before recommending a pace.

entries.name: Vero
entries.summary: A sociable caravan cook who pays attention to water and shared meals.
entries.body: Vero is generous with practical conversation about the caravan's pace and supplies. A simple question about who borrowed a cup is easier to answer than a claim about the whole road.

entries.name: The Hidden Shade Mark
entries.summary: A small chalk mark beneath a town water jar points toward a shaded turn.
entries.body: A chalk crescent under the western water jar points to a shaded turn just off the road. It was drawn small so only someone checking the jar would notice it.

entries.name: Unshared Ledger Detail
entries.summary: A narrator-only continuity detail, not a player-facing fact.
entries.body: A tiny second pinprick beside the market copy is a private continuity clue: the ledger was handled twice, but the mark identifies no person and is not available to the player.
